title: GATE Physics Topic Test: Electromagnetic Theory — Set 2
titleEn: GATE Physics Topic Test: Electromagnetic Theory — Set 2

questions.questionTextEn: What is the Jones vector for right-circularly polarized light (using the $e^{i(kz - \omega t)}$ convention)?
questions.explanationEn: Circular polarization requires equal $x$ and $y$ amplitudes with a $\pm 90^\circ$ ($\pm i$) phase difference; $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(1, i)^T$ has $E_y$ leading $E_x$ by $\pi/2$.

questions.questionTextEn: Inside a uniformly polarized sphere with polarization $\mathbf{P} = P_0 \hat{z}$ (and no free charges), the electric field $\mathbf{E}$ is:
questions.explanationEn: The bound surface charge $\sigma_b = P_0 \cos\theta$ produces a uniform internal depolarization field $\mathbf{E} = -\frac{\mathbf{P}}{3\varepsilon_0}$.

questions.questionTextEn: According to Gauss's law in a linear isotropic dielectric medium, $\nabla \cdot \mathbf{D}$ equals:
questions.explanationEn: The electric displacement $\mathbf{D} = \varepsilon_0 \mathbf{E} + \mathbf{P}$ absorbs bound charge density $\rho_b = -\nabla \cdot \mathbf{P}$, so $\nabla \cdot \mathbf{D} = \rho_{\text{free}}$.

questions.questionTextEn: In a rectangular metallic waveguide with cross-section $a > b$, which mode has the LOWEST cutoff frequency (the dominant mode)?
questions.explanationEn: Cutoff frequency $f_{mn} = \frac{c}{2}\sqrt{(m/a)^2 + (n/b)^2}$. For $a > b$, the smallest non-zero value is $m = 1, n = 0$ ($\text{TE}_{10}$, since $\text{TM}_{10}$ vanishes identically).

questions.questionTextEn: A point charge $+q$ is placed at distance $d$ in front of an infinite grounded conducting plane. The electrostatic force on $+q$ is:
questions.explanationEn: By the method of images, an image charge $-q$ sits at distance $2d$ from $+q$, giving an attractive Coulomb force $F = \frac{q^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 (2d)^2} = \frac{q^2}{16\pi\varepsilon_0 d^2}$.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about a static conductor in electrostatic equilibrium are ALWAYS TRUE?
optionsEn: The electric field inside the bulk of the conductor is identically zero
Any net excess charge resides strictly on the outer surface of the conductor
The electric field just outside the surface is perpendicular to the surface with magnitude $\sigma / \varepsilon_0$
The electrostatic potential varies linearly across the surface of the conductor
questions.explanationEn: Inside a static conductor $\mathbf{E} = 0$ (A), net charge sits on the surface (B), and $\mathbf{E}_{\text{out}} = (\sigma/\varepsilon_0)\hat{n}$ (C). The entire conductor is an equipotential (D is false).

questions.questionTextEn: A cube of side $a$ encloses a point charge $q = 8.854 \times 10^{-12}\text{ C}$ at its exact center. Taking $\varepsilon_0 = 8.854 \times 10^{-12}\text{ F/m}$, what is the total electric flux through ALL six faces combined (in $\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}$)?
questions.explanationEn: By Gauss's law, total flux $\Phi_E = q / \varepsilon_0 = 1\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A uniform magnetic field $\mathbf{B} = 2\hat{z}\text{ T}$ passes through a flat circular loop of area $0.5\text{ m}^2$ whose normal makes an angle of $60^\circ$ with the $z$-axis. What is the magnetic flux through the loop (in Webers)?
questions.explanationEn: $\Phi_B = B A \cos 60^\circ = 2 \times 0.5 \times 0.5 = 0.5\text{ Wb}$.

questions.questionTextEn: Two thin lenses of focal lengths $f_1 = 20\text{ cm}$ and $f_2 = -40\text{ cm}$ are placed in contact. What is the focal length of the combination (in cm)?
questions.explanationEn: $\frac{1}{F} = \frac{1}{20} - \frac{1}{40} = \frac{1}{40} \implies F = 40\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A plane EM wave in vacuum has electric field amplitude $E_0 = 600\text{ V/m}$. Taking $c = 3 \times 10^8\text{ m/s}$, what is its magnetic field amplitude $B_0$ in microtesla ($\mu\text{T}$)?
The electrostatic potential in a region is $V(r) = \frac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{e^{-\alpha r}}{r}$ (screened Coulomb / Yukawa potential). For $r > 0$, what is the volume charge density $\rho(r)$?
questions.explanationEn: For $r > 0$, $\nabla^2\left(\frac{e^{-\alpha r}}{r}\right) = \alpha^2 \frac{e^{-\alpha r}}{r}$. By Poisson's equation $\rho = -\varepsilon_0 \nabla^2 V = -\frac{q \alpha^2}{4\pi}\frac{e^{-\alpha r}}{r}$.

questions.questionTextEn: For a charge distribution with zero net charge ($Q = 0$) and zero net dipole moment ($\mathbf{p} = 0$), but non-zero electric quadrupole moment, how does the electrostatic potential $V(r)$ fall off at large distances $r$?
questions.explanationEn: In the multipole expansion, monopole scales as $1/r$, dipole as $1/r^2$, and quadrupole as $1/r^3$.

questions.questionTextEn: A neutral conducting sphere of radius $R$ is placed in a uniform external electric field $\mathbf{E}_0 = E_0 \hat{z}$. What is the induced surface charge density $\sigma(\theta)$ on the sphere?
questions.explanationEn: The potential outside is $V(r, \theta) = -E_0\left(r - \frac{R^3}{r^2}\right)\cos\theta$. Thus $\sigma(\theta) = -\varepsilon_0\left.\frac{\partial V}{\partial r}\right|_{r=R} = 3\varepsilon_0 E_0 \cos\theta$.

questions.questionTextEn: A parallel-plate capacitor of plate area $A$ and separation $d$ has its lower half ($0 < z < d/2$) filled with a dielectric of permittivity $\varepsilon_1$ and its upper half ($d/2 < z < d$) filled with a dielectric of permittivity $\varepsilon_2$. What is its equivalent capacitance?
questions.explanationEn: The two slabs are in series, each with thickness $d/2$: $C_1 = 2\varepsilon_1 A/d$, $C_2 = 2\varepsilon_2 A/d$. Series combination gives $C = \frac{C_1 C_2}{C_1 + C_2} = \frac{2A}{d}\frac{\varepsilon_1 \varepsilon_2}{\varepsilon_1 + \varepsilon_2}$.

questions.questionTextEn: In relativistic electrodynamics, which of the following statements are TRUE?
optionsEn: If $\mathbf{E} \cdot \mathbf{B} = 0$ and $E < cB$ in one inertial frame, there exists another inertial frame where $\mathbf{E}' = 0$
For a plane electromagnetic wave in vacuum, both invariants $E^2 - c^2 B^2$ and $\mathbf{E} \cdot \mathbf{B}$ are zero
If $\mathbf{E} \cdot \mathbf{B} \neq 0$ in one inertial frame, neither $\mathbf{E}'$ nor $\mathbf{B}'$ can vanish in any inertial frame
If $\mathbf{E} \cdot \mathbf{B} = 0$ and $E > cB$ in one inertial frame, there exists another inertial frame where $\mathbf{B}' = 0$
questions.explanationEn: All four statements follow directly from the invariance of $E^2 - c^2 B^2$ and $\mathbf{E} \cdot \mathbf{B}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A charge $+q$ is placed at distance $d$ from the center of a grounded conducting sphere of radius $R = d / 3$. What is the magnitude of the induced image charge $|q'|$ divided by $q$? (Round to 2 decimal places.)
questions.explanationEn: For a grounded conducting sphere of radius $R$ with external charge $q$ at distance $d$, $q' = -q(R/d) = -q/3$, so $|q'|/q = 1/3 \approx 0.33$.

questions.questionTextEn: An unpolarized beam of intensity $I_0 = 64\text{ W/m}^2$ passes sequentially through three ideal polarizers: the 2nd is at $45^\circ$ to the 1st, and the 3rd is at $45^\circ$ to the 2nd (so $90^\circ$ to the 1st). What is the final transmitted intensity (in $\text{W/m}^2$)?
questions.explanationEn: After 1st: $64/2 = 32$. After 2nd: $32\cos^2 45^\circ = 16$. After 3rd: $16\cos^2 45^\circ = 8\text{ W/m}^2$.

questions.questionTextEn: Two point charges $+q$ and $-q$ are located at $(0, 0, +d)$ and $(0, 0, -d)$ respectively. If $q = 2\text{ nC}$ and $d = 0.05\text{ m}$, what is the magnitude of the electric dipole moment $p$ (in $\text{nC}\cdot\text{m}$)?
questions.explanationEn: Separation between charges is $2d = 0.10\text{ m}$, so $p = q(2d) = 2 \times 0.10 = 0.2\text{ nC}\cdot\text{m}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A circular capacitor of plate radius $R = 0.1\text{ m}$ is charged by a steady current $I = 5\text{ A}$. What is the magnitude of the displacement current (in Amperes) passing through a concentric circular loop of radius $r = 0.05\text{ m}$ between the plates?
questions.explanationEn: Uniform displacement current density gives $I_d(r) = I (r/R)^2 = 5 (0.05 / 0.1)^2 = 5/4 = 1.25\text{ A}$.

questions.questionTextEn: Two long parallel wires separated by $d = 0.1\text{ m}$ carry equal currents $I = 5\text{ A}$ in the same direction. Taking $\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ N/A}^2$, what is the attractive force per unit length between them (in $\mu\text{N/m}$)?
questions.explanationEn: $\frac{F}{L} = \frac{\mu_0 I^2}{2\pi d} = \frac{2 \times 10^{-7} \times 25}{0.1} = 5 \times 10^{-5}\text{ N/m} = 50\,\mu\text{N/m}$.
